# M4-S2: property interfaces lower to Logos_GetF/Logos_SetF accessors (T-203.2).
# A Go package in another workspace module asserts any(&m).(p.Creature),
# reads Logos_GetName, writes Logos_SetHP(5), and the struct holds the
# value. A .lgo package in the same loGo/s module declares
# Orc : p.Creature; reads and writes through the interface reach the
# struct. A third .lgo package asserts the imported conformance, which
# type-checks through the prop facts. The ejected tree keeps the generated
# accessors, go doc lists them on the interface, and the tree stays vet-
# and gofmt-clean.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
mkdir $WORK/bin

# Case 1: everything builds; the Go binary and the .lgo binary print the
# accessor results; the .lgo tests pass.
cd w
logos build ./...
logos build -o $WORK/bin/prop$GOEXE ./g/cmd
exec $WORK/bin/prop$GOEXE
stdout '^name=Trog hp=5$'
logos run ./l/cmdq
stdout '^orc=Orc hp=7 r=6$'
logos test ./...
stdout '^ok\s+example\.com/l/q\s'
cd ..

# Case 2: the ejected tree keeps the generated accessors, runs under plain
# go with identical output, and stays vet- and gofmt-clean; go doc lists
# the accessors on the interface and on the declaring type. Eject runs
# with the workspace off: the l module is self-contained, and eject
# rejects multi-module workspaces.
env GOWORK=off
cd w/l
# Eject takes the non-test tree; case 1 already ran the test.
mv q/q_test.lgo $WORK/q_test.lgo
logos eject -o bout
exists bout/p/p.go
exists bout/q/q.go
exists bout/r/r.go
grep 'Logos_GetName' bout/p/p.go
grep 'Logos_GetHP' bout/p/p.go
grep 'Logos_SetHP' bout/p/p.go
grep 'Logos_GetHP' bout/q/q.go
grep 'Logos_SetHP' bout/q/q.go
cd bout
go run ./cmdq
stdout '^orc=Orc hp=7 r=6$'
go vet ./...
exec $GOROOT/bin/gofmt -l .
! stdout .
go doc example.com/l/p.Creature
stdout 'Logos_GetHP'
stdout 'Logos_GetName'
stdout 'Logos_SetHP'
cd ..
cd ..

-- w/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	./l
	./g
)

-- w/l/go.mod --
module example.com/l

go 1.27

-- w/l/p/p.lgo --
package p

type Creature interface {
	const Name string
	HP int
	Start() error
}

type Monster struct : Creature {
	Name string
	HP   int
}

func (m Monster) Start() error { return nil }

-- w/l/q/q.lgo --
package q

import "example.com/l/p"

type Orc struct : p.Creature {
	Name string
	HP   int
}

func (o Orc) Start() error { return nil }

func Run() string {
	var o Orc
	o.Name = "Orc"
	o.HP = 6
	var c p.Creature = &o
	if got := c.Name; got != "Orc" {
		return "bad-name:" + got
	}
	c.HP += 1
	if o.HP != 7 {
		return "bad-hp"
	}
	return "orc=Orc hp=7"
}

-- w/l/q/q_test.lgo --
package q

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/l/p"
)

func TestThroughInterface(t *testing.T) {
	var o Orc
	o.HP = 1
	var c p.Creature = &o
	c.HP += 6
	if o.HP != 7 {
		t.Fatalf("o.HP = %d, want 7", o.HP)
	}
	if got := any(&o).(p.Creature).Name; got != "" {
		t.Fatalf("Name = %q, want empty", got)
	}
}

-- w/l/r/r.lgo --
package r

import (
	"example.com/l/p"
	"example.com/l/q"
)

var _ p.Creature = &q.Orc{}

func HPOf(o *q.Orc) int {
	var c p.Creature = o
	return c.HP
}

-- w/l/cmdq/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/l/q"
	"example.com/l/r"
)

func main() {
	o := &q.Orc{Name: "Orc", HP: 6}
	fmt.Println(q.Run(), "r="+fmt.Sprint(r.HPOf(o)))
}

-- w/g/go.mod --
module example.com/g

go 1.27

-- w/g/qq/qq.go --
package qq

import "example.com/l/p"

var _ p.Creature = &p.Monster{}

func Run() string {
	m := p.Monster{Name: "Trog"}
	var a any = &m
	c := a.(p.Creature)
	name := c.Logos_GetName()
	c.Logos_SetHP(5)
	if m.HP != 5 {
		return "bad-hp"
	}
	return "name=" + name + " hp=5"
}

-- w/g/cmd/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/g/qq"
)

func main() { fmt.Println(qq.Run()) }
